CVS effects of ageing can be divided into cardiac, vascular, and autonomic changes:

Cardiac changes

Decreased capacity to meet increased demand 

> ↓CO and ↑ Pulse Pressure 
>
> ↑ Myocardial Work 
>
> Blunted Autonomic Responses 
>
> ↑Risk of Comorbidity 

**Autonomic** 

> - ↓ adrenergic receptor density and number
> - ↓Baroreceptor response to ↓pressure 

**Cardiac**

> - ↓maximum heart rate (220-Age)
>
> → Due to fibrosis of the SA node causing reduced pacemaker cell number and function, 
>
> → reduction in catecholamine sensitivity
>
> - SA Node and conduction tissue atrophy
> - LV Hypertrophy due to ↓Aortic Compliance →↑ Afterload 
> - Decreased LV compliance - due to LV hypertrophy and fibrosis 
> - ↑Reliance of Atrial Kick for ventricular filling - up to 30% 

**Pathology**:

↑Risk of: Hypertension, IHD, Arrhythmia 

**Vascular**

> - ↓Arterial compliance due to wall thickening → decreased windkessel effect, 
>
> →↑Systolic ↓Diastolic 
>
> →↑SVR 
>
> → Reduced elastic recoil causes diastolic run off and a fall in diastolic blood pressure

> - ↑Pulmonary arterial pressures - partially due to ↓ LV compliance
> - Impaired Endothelial NO function

**Pathology**:

- increased risk of endothelial dysfunction, atherosclerosis → PVD/IHD
